short: Effects of solid solution and grain-boundary segregation of
title: Effects of solid solution and grain-boundary segregation of Mo on hydrogen embrittlement in 32MnB5 hot-stamping steels

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Ultra-high-strength 32MnB5 hot-stamping steels are susceptible to hydrogen embrittlement. Mo in solid solution and segregated to prior-austenite grain boundaries should reduce hydrogen embrittlement.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/modification), n4 (PRC/treatment), n5 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: In the Mo steel, C, B and Mo segregate to the PAGB; Ti is nearly absent there. Most Mo stays dissolved in the martensite matrix of the Mo steel.

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Mo steel has lower apparent H diffusivity (D_app 6.33 vs 14.2 x10^-11 m2/s) than Ref. H-charged Ref fails by mixed intergranular-cleavage fracture; Mo steel by quasi-cleavage and dimples, no intergranular facets.
states.detail: Absorbed: n10 (PRP/descriptor), n12 (PRP/behavior_class), n15 (MEC/pathway), n16 (MEC/pathway), n17 (MEC/pathway). Premises: H diffusion distance d = sqrt(2Dt): at a given time, distance scales with diffusivity; H atmospheres enhance dislocation mobility and weaken dislocation-obstacle repulsion (HELP) [85-87]; Substitutional solutes exert a drag on moving dislocations (solute-drag effect)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Mo steel keeps far more elongation after H-charging: El_loss ~17/26% vs ~50/79% for Ref

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Mo improves HE resistance of 32MnB5 via PAGB segregation (cohesion) and solid solution (slower H, solute drag)
